acquisitions.title: Bose acquires Skullcandy to help it reach a wider audience
acquisitions.excerpt: Bose has officially announced the acquisition of rival consumer audio company Skullcandy. The two brands recently partnered to integrate Bose technologies, such as active noise cancellation and head-tracking spatial audio, into Skullcandy items like the Method 360 ANC earbuds and Crusher 1080 ANC headphones. Specific financial terms of the agreement were not disclosed in the announcement. Following the buyout, Skullcandy will continue to operate as a separate brand housed within Bose's premium consumer audio division and will maintain its headquarters in Park City, Utah. Bose intends to utilise Skullcandy's distinct branding and designs to reach new demographics and connect with consumers who do not typically prioritise noise cancellation. While Bose products are traditionally popular among frequent travellers and business flyers, Skullcandy's longstanding relationships with board sports athletes offer new avenues for audience growth. Bose CEO Lila Snyder noted that the company is expanding its reach through technology partnerships and a growing portfolio of brands alongside its core products. This purchase follows a series of recent acquisitions by Bose, which bought high-end audio brand McIntosh and subsidiary Sonus faber in 2024, followed by StreamUnlimited Engineering and Firelight Technologies. Additionally, Bose established an in-house content studio called Bose Studios and launched its own record label, Bose Records.

launches.title: Recursive launches Flint, a laptop coding model it says was largely built by AI
launches.excerpt: Artificial intelligence startup Recursive has released its first model, a free laptop coding model called Flint, which was built largely with the assistance of an automated research system known as the Eureka Machine. Led by CEO Richard Socher, the company emerged from stealth in May with $650 million in funding at a valuation of $4.65 billion. The Eureka Machine contributed to nearly every stage of Flint's development, including pretraining, post-training, and inference, allowing a small team to build the model from scratch in under four months. Operating as a mixture-of-experts model, Flint activates only 2.5 billion of its 40 billion parameters at any one time, making it light enough to run locally on a user computer. Because it runs offline, developers can maintain code privacy and avoid cloud service usage fees. Flint is available to download for free on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 open-source licence. In tests on a MacBook Pro with an M4 Pro chip, the model generated approximately 131 tokens per second and outperformed other models with fewer than 50 billion parameters on the SWE-Bench Verified benchmark. Recursive acknowledged that Flint requires more guidance than larger paid coding assistants and suggested that users break large tasks into smaller steps. The company's long-term goal is for the Eureka Machine to achieve full recursive self-improvement under human supervision, with each new model enabling the research system to build subsequent versions more quickly.

launches.title: GM is betting compute and AI will help it compete with Chinese automakers
launches.excerpt: General Motors announced its fourth-generation electric vehicle platform at the annual GM Forward event in New York, focusing heavily on software, central computing, and battery chemistries rather than traditional mechanical performance metrics. The technological overhaul is scheduled to debut in 2028 with the Cadillac Escalade IQ, which will serve as the automaker's technological flagship. Alongside the new platform, GM plans to roll out an autonomous highway driving feature in 2028 that will allow drivers to operate vehicles with their hands and eyes off the road without needing to take over. The company is replacing its old approach of scattering computer chips throughout vehicles with a central compute unit that is forty times more powerful than existing systems. This centralization will eliminate edge chips, trim vehicle wiring by thirty percent, and handle propulsion, chassis controls, active safety, and perception. GM stated that the new central compute unit will also function in fossil fuel models. The automaker is leveraging enterprise artificial intelligence tools to speed up vehicle development, aiming to slash its traditional four- to five-year development timeline in half to better compete with domestic rivals and Chinese manufacturers. Chinese automakers have shortened development cycles to two to three years and maintain a steep cost advantage driven by government subsidies and cheaper labour. By adopting software-defined vehicle strategies, advanced autonomy features, and accelerated digital prototyping, GM hopes to preserve profitability and enhance its competitive standing amidst industry-wide upheaval.

launches.title: While Amazon blocks AI agents, Walmart rolls out the welcome mat
launches.excerpt: Walmart is embracing agentic commerce by launching an Agent Gateway to manage transactions for customers using AI agents. This strategy contrasts with competitors like Amazon and various travel sites that have recently begun blocking AI agents from making purchases on their websites. Announced by Walmart president and CEO John Furner at the Masters of Scale Summit, the initiative builds on existing partnerships with Meta’s Muse, ChatGPT, and Gemini. The new Agent Gateway uses Anthropic's model context protocol to allow approved agents to search inventory and purchase items without accessing personal user information. Additionally, the retailer has developed technology to distinguish agent purchases from customer transactions and provide shoppers with enhanced management tools. Rolling out next month, Agent Profiles will allow customers to authorise individual AI agents, track their purchases separately, and establish spending limits or transaction approvals. Walmart has also introduced specific terms of service for AI agents, ensuring that standard returns policies apply if an agent makes a mistake. Under these terms, agents are barred from exceeding user intentions, accessing direct payment details, or gathering unnecessary data, with non-compliant programmes facing an immediate ban. This support will be available to all Walmart account holders without requiring a paid subscription.

launches.title: AWS Direct Connect announces 100G expansion in Manchester, England
launches.excerpt: Amazon Web Services has announced the expansion of dedicated network connections at its existing Direct Connect location in the Equinix MA3 data centre near Manchester, England. Customers can now access both 10 Gbps and 100 Gbps dedicated connections at the facility, which also includes MACsec encryption capabilities. This development allows businesses and organisations to establish private, direct network access from the Manchester location to all public AWS Regions, with the exception of those located in China, as well as AWS GovCloud Regions and AWS Local Zones. The enhancement makes the Manchester site the third AWS Direct Connect location in England to offer 100 Gbps connections equipped with MACsec encryption. The Direct Connect service is designed to let users create a private, physical network connection linking Amazon Web Services directly with their own internal data centres, corporate offices, or colocation environments. According to the announcement, utilising these private connections can help deliver a more consistent network experience compared to traditional connections routed over the public internet. There are currently more than 150 Direct Connect locations operating worldwide across the global AWS infrastructure network. Further details regarding the global network of locations, alongside guidance on how to purchase and deploy the service, are available through the official product detail pages and getting started resources provided by Amazon Web Services.

launches.title: Beam model by Reflection is now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart and AWS Trainium
launches.excerpt: Beam, the inaugural open weight model from US-based company Reflection, has been made available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart. The model delivers strong performance across various reasoning, coding, and agentic benchmarks. Released under the Apache 2.0 license, Beam is designed for development teams who wish to fine-tune a frontier model for specific domains, modify its weights, and integrate it into their workflows. Users maintain full control over their data and infrastructure while operating the model alongside existing tools in SageMaker AI. Furthermore, Beam has been optimised for AWS Trainium chips to provide a cost-efficient deployment option. Misha Laskin, co-founder and CEO of Reflection, noted that the integration places control directly into developers' hands within their own AWS accounts. Organisations can utilise Beam for tasks such as resolving software issues, generating code, and handling advanced mathematics and science reasoning. Garrett Berntsen, Chief AI Officer at Accenture Federal Services, highlighted that the combination of open weight frontier AI and managed infrastructure offers secure environments with full visibility into data and pipelines. The model is initially accessible in the US East regions of Northern Virginia and Ohio through SageMaker JumpStart endpoints. It is offered in BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 checkpoint variants for deployment via Amazon SageMaker Studio or directly on SageMaker AI.

geo.title: India news: CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka released from Tihar Jail
geo.excerpt: Cockroach Janta Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were released from Tihar Jail on Wednesday after a magistrate declined a police request to extend their judicial custody. The two leaders had been booked for trespassing after raising the Indian flag at the Jantar Mantar protest site, which was previously denotified by Delhi Police. In other domestic news, Union Home Minister Amit Shah criticized the opposition over allegations of electoral irregularities and vote theft regarding the 2024 general elections. Concurrently, opposition leaders and student organisations have been demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar following the removal of millions of names from electoral rolls. In foreign affairs, the Indian foreign ministry reported that one Indian national was killed and three others were injured in attacks on the Dammam airport and the Shaybah oil field in Saudi Arabia. Separately, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk held talks in New Delhi to review bilateral ties and discuss cooperation in trade, defense and technology. In Mumbai, police arrested three more individuals in connection with a shooting at actor Tiger Shroff's car, bringing the total number of arrests to ten. Additionally, Bengaluru-based cybersecurity company eMudhra revoked eight intermediate certificates due to weak private keys, prompting major tech firms to block the affected certificates.

geo.title: Pope Leo will not need further cancer treatment — Vatican
geo.excerpt: Pope Leo XIV will not require further cancer treatment following his diagnosis and surgery last week, according to an announcement from his doctors and the Vatican on Wednesday. The seventy-one-year-old pontiff underwent an operation on October 13 at Rome's Gemelli hospital to remove the lower lobe of his right lung after publicly disclosing his condition during a Sunday blessing on October 11. Final histopathology and molecular testing reports issued on Wednesday confirmed that the tumour was a lung adenocarcinoma and that the disease was entirely localised. Following these results, an oncological assessment established that no further therapeutic measures, such as chemotherapy or radiotherapy, are necessary. The pope's surgeon stated that there is no clinical reason to cancel the pontiff's upcoming visit to South America, which is scheduled for November and includes stops in Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. Pope Leo was discharged from hospital on Saturday and has indicated that he intends to resume his duties gradually following the procedure.

geo.title: Airbnb guests freed from chores involving ‘significant effort’ under new global rules
geo.excerpt: Airbnb hosts will no longer be permitted to require guests to complete tasks that demand significant effort or time under updated global rules taking effect on 20 November. The platform acted following long-standing complaints from users who were charged substantial cleaning fees while still being asked to handle extensive chores. Under the revised policy, hosts will generally be barred from demanding that guests strip bed linen, take rubbish offsite, or wash and put away dishes. While guests can no longer be ordered to clean dishes, hosts remain able to ask for used items to be placed into the sink. The changes also limit hosts to setting seven standard house rules that must be displayed fully at the time of booking. Permitted house rules include specified check-in and check-out times, guest limits, smoking restrictions, quiet hours, and pet policies. Additionally, hosts may introduce other reasonable requests based on relevant local considerations. Examples of acceptable local requests include asking visitors to limit shower durations due to water shortages or disposing of rubbish securely in animal-proof containers. Cleaning fees have not been shown to guests since April 2025, with hosts instead permitted to incorporate those costs into the overall price of the stay. An Airbnb spokesperson stated that the redesign aims to address community feedback regarding confusing and onerous house rules by making expectations clearer and preventing unexpected demands.

geo.title: Russia and Ukraine trade strikes overnight as Moscow signals readiness for peace talks
geo.excerpt: Russia and Ukraine engaged in major drone and missile strikes overnight following diplomatic meetings involving US envoy Steve Witkoff in Saint Petersburg and Oslo. US President Donald Trump stated that negotiations were the closest they had ever been to ending the war, while the Kremlin indicated it was open in principle to resuming trilateral talks with the United States and Ukraine in mid-November. Despite the diplomatic engagement, attacks continued across multiple regions, with Kyiv reporting injuries and damage to metro infrastructure from drone barrages. Moscow's mayor reported that hundreds of drones had been launched toward the Russian region, resulting in two injuries after interceptions. Meanwhile, Ukrainian authorities reported deaths from Russian strikes in Sumy, Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, and Donetsk. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov noted that Russia wanted upcoming talks to focus on post-war security, although Moscow expressed doubts regarding the substance of Ukrainian and European peace proposals delivered by the US envoy. Preparations were also underway for a historic summit in China next month involving Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump, and Xi Jinping. During his meeting with Putin, Witkoff praised the Russian president for freeing detained US citizen Stephen Hubbard, a move that prompted Trump to delay economic sanctions on Russia. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed that Kyiv also supported the resumption of trilateral discussions as soon as possible.

geo.title: US orders some diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia amid Houthi threat
geo.excerpt: At least two people were killed and eight others injured in a strike on King Fahd International Airport in the eastern Saudi city of Dammam on Wednesday. The Saudi Civil Aviation Authority reported that the attack caused operational disruptions and forced flights to be diverted, though officials did not immediately identify who was behind the strike and the Houthi rebels did not claim responsibility. Earlier on the same day, the Saudi Energy Ministry stated that falling debris from an intercepted drone targeting an oil facility killed two foreign nationals, specifically a Filipino and a Nepali citizen, and injured two others. These incidents occurred as the revived conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Iranian-backed Houthi rebels has intensified in recent weeks, leading to near-daily attacks following the collapse of a four-year truce. In response to the escalating security situation, the United States State Department ordered the departure of non-essential staff and family members from the US embassy in Riyadh. US State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott cited increased hostilities by Iranian-supported Houthis against civilian airports and critical infrastructure as the reason for the directive. Pigott also denied broader media reports suggesting that similar departure orders had been issued for US diplomatic posts in other Gulf nations such as the United Arab Emirates, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain. The US government has issued similar evacuation orders multiple times this year amid regional hostilities and retaliatory strikes.

invest.title: Why this JPMorgan strategist thinks the stock market’s tailspin might have run its course
invest.excerpt: JPMorgan strategists have concluded that the recent downward trend in the stock market may be nearing its end. This assessment is based on the observation that hedge fund positioning has decreased significantly since reaching a peak in September. According to the financial firm's analysis, the reduction in aggressive short positions and overall exposure suggests that much of the immediate selling pressure has already occurred. The strategists argue that this substantial de-risking process creates a more stable foundation for equities moving forward. Because institutional investors have already adjusted their portfolios to account for prevailing economic uncertainties, the remaining downside risk for the broader stock market appears constrained. This outlook contrasts with the heightened volatility and cautious sentiment that characterised trading patterns earlier in the autumn. While the strategists do not guarantee an immediate and sustained rally, their assessment indicates that the market has absorbed a considerable amount of negative sentiment. The shift in hedge fund behaviour is viewed as a key indicator of market resilience following the recent tailspin. Consequently, the analysis implies that equities may be better positioned to weather upcoming macroeconomic data releases and central bank policy decisions without experiencing the same severe corrections seen in recent weeks.

invest.title: Comcast beats earnings expectations as media revenue offsets weakness in connectivity
invest.excerpt: Comcast exceeded Wall Street expectations for its third-quarter earnings, bolstered by strong performance in its media unit despite challenges in its theme parks business. The Peacock streaming service achieved a quarterly profit for only the second time since its 2020 launch, recording $261 million in adjusted earnings on $1.8 billion in revenue. This growth was aided by high viewership for the FIFA World Cup across NBCUniversal platforms. Overall, revenue in the media division increased by 13 percent to $5.4 billion. In contrast, the connectivity and platforms sector experienced a 2.7 percent decline in year-over-year revenue. Domestic broadband residential customers decreased by 144,000, and cable customers fell by 274,000, while the mobile business gained 368,000 subscribers. Meanwhile, theme park revenue dropped 4.4 percent to $2.6 billion due to cyclical headwinds and promotional activities affecting admissions. Net income for the period rose to $3.45 billion, compared with $3.33 billion in the corresponding period of the previous year. Comcast previously announced plans to spin off NBCUniversal and Sky into a separate publicly traded company, following the separation of several cable networks and digital businesses into Versant earlier in the year.

invest.title: Procter & Gamble earnings beat as sales rise 4%, boosted by laundry and home products
invest.excerpt: Procter and Gamble reported fiscal first-quarter earnings and revenue that exceeded analysts' expectations, driven by rising demand for laundry detergent and home care products. Company shares increased by more than two percent in premarket trading following the announcement. Net income attributable to the company reached 4.73 billion dollars, or 1.97 dollars per share, compared with 4.75 billion dollars, or 1.95 dollars per share, in the previous year. On an adjusted basis, excluding restructuring costs and other items, earnings stood at 2 dollars per share. The company recorded an overall volume growth of 2.4 percent for the quarter. Executives noted continued signs of a bifurcated economy, where high-income consumers purchase premium items while lower-income shoppers manage tighter budgets. Fabric and home care performed best among divisions with a volume increase of 4.3 percent, whereas health care volume declined by 2.9 percent and grooming dropped by 0.4 percent. Looking ahead, Procter and Gamble reiterated its core earnings per share forecast between 6.89 dollars and 7.11 dollars for fiscal 2027. The all-in sales growth projection was revised upward to a range of 2 percent to 4 percent, largely reflecting the recent acquisition of supplements brand Thorne.

invest.title: France protests: Macron condemns 'stupid' comments from Trump, others as bond-market pressure builds
invest.excerpt: French President Emmanuel Macron has criticised foreign leaders, including United States President Donald Trump, for making unacceptable and stupid comments following mass protests and rioting in France. Trump and other Republican figures had blamed the unrest on migrants, jihadists and Communists while campaigning ahead of upcoming midterms, while Iranian officials also weighed in by calling on Macron to listen to the demonstrators. The protests, initially triggered by student demonstrations over public services and the cost of living, have involved looting, arson and solidarity marches in several European countries. French authorities have announced that some military forces will be deployed to help maintain order as student unions and the yellow vest group call for further weekend rallies. This social and political volatility has been compounded by an emerging fiscal crisis that pushed France's benchmark government borrowing cost to a 24-year high on Thursday. The yield on 10-year French government bonds rose to 5.113 percent, surpassing the 10-year United States Treasury yield for the first time since 2013 as investors remain skeptical about fiscal consolidation. Parliament is currently debating the 2027 budget, and the government lacks a majority, raising the possibility of special powers that could stoke further political instability. Morningstar has estimated insured losses from the unrest at up to 1.2 billion euros, while the government has recently revised its 2026 real gross domestic product growth forecast down to 0.5 percent. Economists warn that prolonged protests could weigh on household and business confidence, further dampening economic activity and exacerbating fiscal pressures.

invest.title: Brent crude tops $111 on Middle East worries as U.S., Israel reportedly weigh fresh Iran strikes
invest.excerpt: Oil prices increased on Thursday due to growing concerns over a potential escalation in the Middle East conflict. Brent crude futures rose by 2.68% to reach $111.74 a barrel early in the morning, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude gained 2.21% to trade at $99.30. Reports indicate that the United States and Israeli militaries have formulated specific plans for renewed strikes against Iran following the upcoming midterm elections. According to unnamed U.S. officials cited in media reports, planning for a short and intensive military operation is currently progressing. Concurrently, the United States government ordered non-emergency employees and their families to depart from Saudi Arabia. State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott clarified in a social media post that this directive applies exclusively to Saudi Arabia due to mounting attacks by Iran-aligned Houthi forces on civilian infrastructure. Despite the rising energy costs, market analysts suggest that the broader economic fallout may prove less severe than in past decades. Experts point out that modern consumers are generally less vulnerable to energy shocks, with inflation-adjusted crude prices remaining well below historical highs. Government data indicates that gasoline currently accounts for approximately half of the disposable income share it represented a decade ago. This shift suggests that households are better positioned to absorb the impact of elevated energy prices without severe financial disruption.
